body: What ≤ 5 µm flatness tolerance actually means at FOM SD 500's full 500 mm width.
Holding tight flatness tolerance gets harder as coating width increases, since even small deviations across a wider surface compound into visible film non-uniformity.

FOM SD 500 holds ≤ 5 µm flatness across its entire surface despite being the largest standard-size head in the steel series, which is what keeps coatings uniform at the full 500 mm width rather than only at narrower settings. That precision pairs with a genuinely wide viscosity range, 1 cP up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C, so the same head that coats a thin printed electronics ink can also handle a heavy battery slurry without needing separate hardware for each. Chemically passivated stainless steel 1.4404 construction keeps that precision intact over repeated use, resisting the corrosion that varied ink and slurry chemistries could otherwise introduce over time.

faqs.question: What is the FOM SD 50 used for?
faqs.answer: It's a compact stainless-steel slot-die coating head for precision coating from 1 to 50 mm, used across batteries, fuel cells, photovoltaics, and printed electronics.

faqs.question: What viscosity range does it support?
faqs.answer: 1 cP to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C, covering thin solutions through thick slurries on the same head.

faqs.question: How flat is the coating head internally?
faqs.answer: Flatness tolerance on inside planes holds to ≤ 5 μm across the entire surface, supporting uniform coatings.

faqs.question: Is it compatible with all FOM coating machines?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's designed to work seamlessly with the full FOM coating machine range.

faqs.question: Does it support double-sided coating?
faqs.answer: Yes, when used on the FOM moduloR2R machine.

faqs.question: Can it be used with or without a meniscus guide?
faqs.answer: Yes, the design adapts either way depending on the application.

faqs.question: How easy is the head to maintain?
faqs.answer: Its lightweight, sturdy design supports easy assembly, disassembly, cleaning, and maintenance.

faqs.question: Does it minimize material waste?
faqs.answer: Yes, a low dead-volume design reduces material waste during coating runs.

faqs.question: What connection types are available?
faqs.answer: Threaded connections suited to various tubing sizes, in both standard and high-viscosity versions.

faqs.question: How is the SD 50 different from the SD 25?
faqs.answer: SD 50 covers a wider coating width range, 1 to 50 mm versus SD 25's 1 to 25 mm, while sharing the same viscosity range, flatness tolerance, and machine compatibility.

faqs.question: What is the price of the FOM SD 50 in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the shim, guide, and connection configuration needed.

body.text: FOM SD 50 is a compact stainless-steel slot-die head designed to work seamlessly with all FOM coating machines.
Coating width covers 1 to 50 mm, extending beyond the narrowest formats to a wider working range on the same platform.
Viscosity compatibility spans 1 cP up to over 100,000 cPs at 25°C, covering thin solutions through thick slurries on the same head.
Inside plane flatness tolerance holds to ≤ 5 μm across the entire surface, ensuring consistent coatings at the wider format.
Threaded connections accommodate various tubing sizes, available in both standard and high-viscosity versions.
A lightweight yet sturdy design keeps assembly, disassembly, and maintenance straightforward, without compromising structural integrity or performance.
A low dead-volume design minimizes material waste, valuable when working with precious or expensive precursor materials.
The head adapts with or without a meniscus guide, and precise FOM alignment design keeps shim and meniscus guide positioning reliable across setups.
Double-sided coating is supported when used on the FOM moduloR2R machine.
A lightweight, high-quality protective flight case ships with the head for shipping and storage.

body: A slot-die head that's difficult to clean or reassemble slows down every formulation change, and formulation research often means changing materials often.
FOM SD 50's lightweight yet sturdy design keeps assembly, disassembly, cleaning, and maintenance straightforward, without asking the operator to sacrifice structural performance for convenience.
A low dead-volume design compounds that speed advantage: less material sits trapped in the head between runs, meaning less waste and less cleaning residue to deal with when switching formulations.
Quick and easy installation across any FOM coating machine means the head itself is rarely the bottleneck in a busy research schedule.
